frontier.hypothesis: increase base's reg_n_refs via a legitimate additional use in the loop body — e.g. compute `count` initialization from base explicitly, or duplicate `new_var = base + word_offset` into a real second use — to make GCC's allocator prefer $s4 over the $a0 copy-prop alias at insn #18
frontier.mechanism: GCC's local-alloc uses reg_n_refs as a tiebreaker; more references to `base` should raise its priority for allocation and picking-at-use per [[duplicated-statement-into-arms]] (2026-07-01 sanction for legitimate duplication effects)
frontier.next_probe: s3 (structural): duplicate the `new_var = (s32)base + word_offset` computation once outside the loop (byte-neutral shape TBD), or replace the standalone `count = *(p++)` with `count = *(u32*)(base_addr + word_offset); p = (u32*)(base_addr + word_offset + 4);` to add a second explicit base reference in the pre-loop block

frontier.hypothesis: the `s32 buf[8]` unused array is providing frame reservation that is NOT needed for the discarded-return spill (GCC schedules `sw v0, 0x10(sp)` because target has such a slot; removing buf shrinks frame and drops the spill, but may not affect insn #18)
frontier.mechanism: isolate whether the frame reservation is load-bearing for the score by removing buf[8] AND measuring whether the discarded-return sw disappears; this determines whether the WRITTEN-never-read carve-out is required for the closing form
frontier.next_probe: s3 (structural/policy): remove `s32 buf[8]` and `(void)buf;` from H1d, sandbox, disasm — if the sw v0,0x10(sp) survives (via GCC's own frame allocation for register saves) the buf[8] is decorative and can be dropped; if it disappears the buf[8] is providing real frame semantics and a WRITTEN-never-read form (with actual stores) is required per [[dead-vars-local-array]] 2026-07-01 carve-out
